1.title: Number systems and place value
tasks: Place −3, 0.45, 1/2 and 2.1 on one number line. Then order them from least to greatest.
A clinic orders 198 boxes with 24 masks per box. Estimate first, then calculate the exact number of masks. Explain whether your estimate is reasonable.
A number rounds to 3,700 to the nearest hundred and to 3,650 to the nearest ten. Determine every possible whole number.
Use the digits 0, 2, 4 and 7 exactly once to make two two-digit numbers whose positive difference is as small as possible. Prove no smaller positive difference is possible.

1.title: Powers, expanded form and order of operations
tasks: Evaluate 3² + 2³ × 5 − √81. Show the order of operations.
A square display has 2⁵ lights in each row and 2⁴ rows. Write the total as a single power of 2 and as a whole number.
Insert one pair of brackets into 18 − 6 ÷ 3 + 2 so that the value is 6. Verify your expression.
Find all whole numbers n for which n² + n is a two-digit number ending in 2. Justify that your list is complete.

1.title: Factors, multiples and primes
tasks: Write 360 as a product of prime factors. Hence find the number of factor pairs of 360.
Three warning lights flash every 18 s, 24 s and 30 s. They flash together at 09:00:00. When do they next flash together?
Two numbers have HCF 12 and LCM 420. One number is 60. Find the other and verify both conditions.
Find the smallest positive integer that leaves remainder 1 when divided by 2, 3, 4 and 5, but is divisible by 7. Explain your search.

1.title: Fractions and decimals
tasks: Calculate 3/4 − 5/12 + 0.375. Give an exact fraction and a decimal.
A 2.4 L jug is 5/8 full. Then 0.35 L is poured out. What fraction of the jug’s capacity remains?
Without a calculator, decide which is larger: 17/23 or 23/31. Show a comparison that does not use decimal approximations.
A fraction becomes 2/3 when 3 is added to numerator and denominator, and 1/2 when 2 is subtracted from both. Find the original fraction.

1.title: Percentages and applications
tasks: A price of 48,000 FCFA is reduced by 15%, then increased by 15%. Find the final price and percentage change from the original.
A market budget is split 35% food, 25% transport, 15% books and the rest savings. If savings are 30,000 FCFA, find the total budget.
Shop A offers 25% off. Shop B offers 20% off and then 5% off. Compare the final multipliers and explain which is cheaper.
After a 20% increase, what percentage decrease returns a quantity to its original value? Generalise for an increase of p%.

1.title: Patterns, expressions and equations
tasks: For 5, 9, 13, 17, … write a term-to-term rule and an nth-term rule. Find term 50.
A taxi charge is 900 FCFA plus 350 FCFA per kilometre. Write a formula for C kilometres k, then find k when C=4,400.
A student claims 4(x+3)=4x+3. Use an area model or numerical counterexample, then state the correct identity.
A growing pattern uses 4, 10, 18, 28, … tiles. Find a rule for term n and justify it from first differences.

1.title: Lines, angles, triangles and constructions
tasks: Two parallel lines are cut by a transversal. One obtuse angle is 124°. Determine all acute angles and explain the angle facts used.
A triangular roof has angles in the ratio 2:3:4. Find the three angles and classify the triangle.
Can lengths 4.2 cm, 6.1 cm and 10.4 cm form a triangle? Justify without drawing.
A regular polygon has exterior angle 24°. Find its number of sides and sum of interior angles. Explain why 24° must divide 360°.

1.title: Sets and classification
tasks: In a class of 32, 18 study French, 15 study Spanish and 7 study both. Complete a Venn diagram and find how many study neither.
Let U={1,…,20}, A=multiples of 3 and B=factors of 18. List A∩B and A∪B.
If |A|=19, |B|=17 and |A∪B|=28, find |A∩B| and explain the inclusion–exclusion step.
Three clubs have 12, 13 and 14 members. Each pair shares 5 members and 2 students are in all three. If 30 students join at least one club, is the information consistent? Justify.

1.title: Perimeter, area, surface area and volume
tasks: A 12 cm by 8 cm rectangle has a 3 cm by 3 cm square cut from one corner. Find the remaining area and perimeter.
A closed cuboid is 40 cm by 25 cm by 30 cm. Find its capacity in litres and its external surface area.
Two rectangles have perimeter 40 cm. Compare the areas of 2 cm×18 cm and 10 cm×10 cm. What do you conjecture?
An open-top box is made by cutting 2 cm squares from each corner of a 20 cm by 14 cm card. Find its volume and the fraction of card area removed.

1.title: Data, tables and graphs
tasks: For 4, 7, 7, 8, 9, 10, 10, 10, 15 find mean, median, mode and range.
A pie-chart sector of 72° represents 18 students. Find the class size and the angle for 27 students.
A graph of water use starts its vertical axis at 96 L. Values 98 L and 102 L appear four times apart. Explain the visual distortion and redesign the scale.
Five whole numbers have median 8, unique mode 6 and mean 8. Find one possible set, then determine the smallest possible range.

2.title: Ratios and equivalent ratios
tasks: Simplify 84:126 and write two equivalent ratios.
Share 168,000 FCFA in the ratio 3:4:5.
A drink uses syrup:water=2:7. Is adding 100 mL syrup and 350 mL water to any batch guaranteed to preserve the taste? Explain.
Red:blue is 3:5. After 8 red counters are added it is 7:10. Find the original counts.

2.title: Proportional reasoning
tasks: If y is directly proportional to x and y=18 when x=12, find the constant and y when x=35.
A map scale is 1:25,000. A path is 7.6 cm on the map. Find its actual length in kilometres.
The points (2,7), (5,17.5), (8,28) lie on a line. Explain two tests showing the relationship is proportional.
Twelve workers complete a task in 15 days at equal rates. After 5 days, 2 workers leave. How many more days are needed?

2.title: Rates and unit rates
tasks: A cyclist covers 42 km in 1 h 45 min. Find average speed in km/h.
Rice costs 8,400 FCFA for 6 kg or 11,200 FCFA for 8.5 kg. Find each unit price and the better buy.
A tap fills 3/5 of a tank in 24 min. At constant flow, how long for the remaining tank? Explain using a unit rate.
Two printers together print 900 pages in 12 min. Printer A prints 20 pages/min more than B. Find both rates.

2.title: Integers and operations
tasks: Temperature falls 2.5°C per hour from 6°C for 7 hours, then rises 4°C. Find the final temperature.
Explain with a number-line pattern why (−5)(−3)=15.
Find all integer pairs (a,b) with a+b=−2 and ab=−15.

2.title: Algebraic expressions and equations
tasks: Simplify 4(2x−3)−3(x+5), then evaluate at x=−2.
Plan A costs 2,500+600d FCFA; Plan B costs 4,300+450d. Find the break-even distance d.
Solve 3(2x−1)=2(x+5)+7 and check by substitution.
The perimeter of a rectangle is 50 cm. Its length is 5 cm more than twice its width. Find its dimensions.

2.title: Numerical patterns and generalisation
tasks: Find the nth term of 11,17,23,… and determine whether 305 is a term.
Stage n has a row of n squares sharing sides. Find the number of matchsticks and explain your rule.
Compare aₙ=5n+2 and bₙ=3n+20. Find when they are equal and which is greater afterwards.
A sequence starts 2,6,12,20,30. Use differences to find a formula and predict term 50.

2.title: 2D geometry: angles, perimeter and area
tasks: The angles of a quadrilateral are x, 2x, 3x and 4x. Find all angles.
A running track is a rectangle 60 m by 30 m with a semicircle on each short end. Find perimeter and area in terms of π.
A triangle has area 54 cm² and base 12 cm. A similar triangle has scale factor 3/2. Find its height and area.
A rectangle has area 96 cm² and integer side lengths. Which dimensions minimise perimeter? Justify by checking factor pairs.

2.title: 3D geometry: solids, surface area and volume
tasks: Find total surface area and volume of a cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 10 cm, in exact form.
A tank 1.2 m×0.8 m×0.75 m is 65% full. How many litres does it contain?
A cube’s side doubles. Explain the factors by which surface area and volume change.
A closed cuboid has volume 216 cm³ and integer sides. Compare 6×6×6 and 3×6×12 to find which uses less material.

2.title: Transformations and symmetry
tasks: Translate A(−2,3) by vector (5,−4), then reflect the image in the y-axis.
Triangle vertices (1,1),(5,1),(1,3) are enlarged scale factor −1/2 about the origin. Give image coordinates.
Describe a single transformation mapping (x,y) to (−y,x). State its invariant point.
Two successive reflections are in parallel vertical lines x=1 and x=4. Describe their combined transformation and justify with one test point.

2.title: Probability and simulation
tasks: A bag has 5 red, 3 blue and 2 green counters. Find P(not blue) and P(red or green).
Two fair coins are tossed. List the sample space and find P(exactly one head).
A game wins 4 points with probability 1/3 and loses 1 point otherwise. Find expected score and assess fairness.
A biased spinner gives P(A)=2P(B)=4P(C). Find all three probabilities.

2.title: Univariate data
tasks: For 3,5,6,7,8,8,9,12,14 find median, quartiles and IQR using the median-excluded convention.
Class A has median 68 and IQR 12; Class B median 72 and IQR 25. Compare centre and spread without claiming more than the summaries show.
The mean of eight values is 14. One value recorded as 31 should be 13. Find the corrected mean.
Construct seven integer data values with range 10, median 8, mean 8 and no mode.

3.title: The real number system
tasks: Classify −7, 0.125, √11 and π as integer, rational or irrational, using the most specific set.
Give rational bounds of width 0.01 containing √7.
Prove that 0.272727… is rational by converting it to a fraction.
Prove that √3 is irrational using contradiction and divisibility by 3.

3.title: Powers, roots and scientific notation
tasks: Simplify (3x⁴y⁻²)(6x⁻¹y⁵) with positive exponents.
A cell is 7.2×10⁻⁶ m wide. How many fit across 3.6 cm?
Compare 5³⁰ and 3⁵⁰ without fully evaluating; justify using a common exponent.

3.title: Functions, expressions and algebraic reasoning
tasks: For f(x)=2x²−3, find f(−2), f(a+1), and solve f(x)=15.
Factor fully 6x²−15x and hence solve 6x²−15x=0.
A function maps x→3x−4. Explain why every real output has exactly one real input and find the inverse rule.
Find integers a,b such that x²+ax+b has roots differing by 5 and product −14.

3.title: Linear relationships and graphs
tasks: Find the equation of the line through (−2,5) and (4,−7).
A tank contains 820 L and drains at 35 L/min. Write a model and find when 120 L remain.
Lines y=3x−4 and 6x−2y=8 look different. Determine their relationship algebraically.
Find k so the line kx+2y=7 is perpendicular to y=4x−1.

3.title: Equations, inequalities and systems
tasks: Solve 4−3(2x−5)≤25 and show the solution on a number line.
Adult tickets cost 4,000 FCFA and student tickets 2,500 FCFA. 86 tickets earn 275,000 FCFA. Find each number.
Classify the system 2x+3y=7 and 4x+6y=15 as one, none or infinitely many solutions. Explain.
Find all integer points satisfying x≥0, y≥0, x+y≤6 and 2x+y≥8.

3.title: Transformations, congruence and symmetry
tasks: Rotate P(3,−1) 90° clockwise about (1,2).
State the minimum data needed for SSS, SAS and ASA congruence tests.
Explain why AAA proves similarity but not congruence, with a counterexample.
A translation followed by its inverse leaves every point fixed. Show this using vectors.

3.title: Similarity, proof and trigonometry
tasks: A right triangle has legs 9 cm and 12 cm. Find hypotenuse and both acute angles.
A 1.6 m person casts a 2.4 m shadow while a tree casts 13.5 m. Find tree height.
Prove that the altitude to the hypotenuse creates two triangles similar to the original.
From point A, angle of elevation to a tower is 28°. After moving 20 m closer it is 41°. Form equations and find the tower height to 3 s.f.

3.title: Three-dimensional solids and measurement
tasks: Find volume and surface area of a cone with r=5 cm, h=12 cm.
A 330 mL cylindrical can has radius 3.2 cm. Find its required internal height.
Measurements 8.4 cm and 5.2 cm are to nearest 0.1 cm. Give error bounds for their product.
A sphere fits exactly inside a cube. Find the fraction of cube volume occupied by the sphere.

3.title: Bivariate data, correlation and causation
tasks: For points (1,2),(2,4),(3,5),(4,8), describe direction, form and strength without calculating r.
A line of best fit is y=1.8x+12 for study hours x and score y. Interpret both parameters and predict at x=7.
Ice-cream sales and sunburn cases correlate. Explain a plausible confounder and why correlation is not causation.
A point far to the right follows the trend. Explain how high leverage can strengthen or weaken a fitted correlation.

3.title: Probability, sampling and evidence
tasks: A bag has 4 red and 6 blue. Two are drawn without replacement. Find P(two red).
A test has sensitivity 90% and specificity 95%. In 1,000 people, prevalence is 2%. Build a frequency tree and find P(disease|positive).
Compare a voluntary online poll with a stratified random sample for estimating school opinion.
Events A,B have P(A)=0.6, P(B)=0.5, P(A∪B)=0.8. Find P(A∩B), P(A|B), and test independence.

4.title: Number Foundations: Exponents, Surds and Accuracy
tasks: Simplify √72−2√8 and rationalise 5/√3.
A length is 12.4 cm to nearest 0.1 cm. Give bounds for the area of a square with this side.
Show that (2+√3)(2−√3)=1 and explain the conjugate strategy.
Find all integers n for which √(n+6)−√n=1.

4.title: Algebraic Expressions and Factorisation
tasks: Factor fully 6x³−15x²−36x.
Simplify (x²−9)/(x²−x−6), stating exclusions.
Prove (a+b)²−(a−b)²=4ab geometrically or algebraically.
Factor x⁴−5x²+4 completely and solve when it is zero.

4.title: Linear Equations, Inequalities and Systems
tasks: Solve |2x−5|<7.
A blend contains coffee at 3,200 and 5,000 FCFA/kg. Make 18 kg worth 4,200 FCFA/kg. Find masses.
For what k does kx+2y=5 and 6x+4y=9 have no solution?
Find all integer solutions of 3x+5y=41 with x,y≥0.

4.title: Functions, Coordinates and Linear Models
tasks: Find the line perpendicular to 2x−3y=12 through (4,−1).
A fare is linear: 3 km costs 2,100 FCFA and 11 km costs 5,700 FCFA. Model cost and interpret intercept.
Find domain and range of f(x)=√(9−x²).
A line cuts positive axes at (a,0),(0,b) and passes through (3,4). Find integer a,b>0 with smallest a+b.

4.title: Quadratic Expressions and Equations
tasks: Solve 3x²−5x−2=0 by factorisation and formula.
A rectangle has area 96 m² and length 4 m more than width. Find dimensions.
Determine k so x²−6x+k=0 has one repeated root; connect to vertex form.
If roots of x²−7x+10=0 are α,β, find α²+β² without solving.

4.title: Quadratic Functions and Graphical Reasoning
tasks: Write y=2x²−8x+3 in vertex form and state vertex and axis.
A projectile has h=−5t²+20t+1. Find maximum height and when it hits ground.
Compare y=x² and y=(x−3)²−4 as transformations.
Find the range of k for which y=x²+kx+9 has no real zeros.

4.title: Patterns, Sequences and Generalisation
tasks: Find the nth term of 4,11,22,37,56 using differences.
A theatre has 24 seats in row 1 and 4 more each row. Find row 20 and total through row 20.
Given Sₙ=3n²+2n, derive uₙ and classify the sequence.
A sequence satisfies u₁=5, uₙ₊₁=2uₙ−3. Transform vₙ=uₙ−3 and find explicit uₙ.

4.title: Growth and Financial Mathematics
tasks: An investment of 250,000 FCFA grows 6% annually for 4 years. Find its value.
A machine depreciates 18% yearly from 8,000,000 FCFA. When does it first fall below 4,000,000?
Explain why +12% then −12% is a net decrease and calculate it.
Two plans start at 100,000 FCFA. A adds 20,000 yearly; B grows 12% yearly. Find the first year B exceeds A.

4.title: Congruence, Similarity and Transformations
tasks: A shape is enlarged scale factor −2 about (1,−1). Find the image of P(4,3).
Similar solids have surface areas 54 and 150 cm². Find linear scale factor and volume ratio.
Prove diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other using congruent triangles.
Find the centre of enlargement mapping A(1,2)→A′(5,8) and B(3,2)→B′(9,8).

4.title: Pythagoras, Trigonometry and Measurement
tasks: A cuboid is 6×8×24 cm. Find its space diagonal.
From a point 45 m from a tower, elevation is 37°. Find height to 3 s.f.
Derive tan θ=sin θ/cos θ from right-triangle definitions.
A ship sails 18 km east then 24 km on bearing 150°. Find displacement and bearing from start.

4.title: Surface Area and Volume
tasks: Find volume and total area of a hemisphere radius 6 cm including its base.
A cone and cylinder share radius and height. Compare volumes and explain.
A solid is enlarged by k. Its volume rises 72.8%. Find k and area percentage rise.
A closed cylinder has volume 500π cm³. Express area in r and find the radius minimising it.

4.title: Statistics: Distributions and Data
tasks: For grouped classes 0–10,10–20,20–30 with frequencies 4,9,7 estimate the mean.
Two box plots have medians 52,55 and IQRs 8,20. Make a careful comparison.
Explain why median and IQR may be preferable for skewed income data.
The mean of 12 values is 18 and standard deviation 4. Every value is transformed by y=3x−5. Find new mean and standard deviation.

4.title: Probability: Combined Events
tasks: A fair die is rolled twice. Find P(sum 8).
A factory has 3% defects; a check catches 92% of defects and falsely flags 4% of good items. Find P(defect|flagged).
Give an example of mutually exclusive events that are not independent and prove it numerically.
Without replacement from 5 red,4 blue,3 green, find P(three drawn are all different).

5.title: Polynomials, Factor Theorem and Algebraic Fractions
tasks: Divide 2x³−3x²−11x+6 by x−3 and factor completely.
Solve (x+1)/(x−2)=3/(x+2), stating exclusions.
Prove the remainder on division by x−a is f(a).
Find k so x³−4x²+kx+6 has factor x−2, then factor completely.

5.title: Functions: Transformations, Composites and Inverses
tasks: For f(x)=2x−3 and g(x)=x²+1 find f∘g and g∘f.
Find inverse of h(x)=(3x+4)/(x−2), with restrictions.
Explain why f(x)=x² on real numbers has no inverse function, then restrict its domain.
Solve f(f(x))=x for f(x)=1−2x.

5.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
tasks: Solve 3^(2x−1)=20 using logarithms.
A culture grows continuously from 500 at 18% per hour. Find population after 7 h and doubling time.
Derive log_b(MN)=log_b M+log_b N from exponent definitions.
Solve log₂x+log₂(x−2)=3, checking domain.

5.title: Sequences and Series
tasks: An arithmetic sequence has u₄=17,u₁₀=41. Find u₁,d and S₂₅.
An annuity pays 50,000 FCFA at each year-end into 6% interest for 8 years. Find value immediately after final payment.
A geometric series converges to 30 and first term is 12. Find r and justify convergence.
Given u₁=4,uₙ₊₁=uₙ+2n+3, derive an explicit formula.

5.title: Quadratic Inequalities and Linear Programming
tasks: Solve x²−5x−14≤0.
Maximise P=40x+55y subject to x≥0,y≥0,2x+y≤18,x+3y≤21.
Explain why a linear objective over a bounded polygon reaches an optimum at a vertex.
Repeat the optimisation for integer x,y and state whether the continuous optimum is feasible.

5.title: Circle Geometry and Geometric Proof
tasks: An angle at the centre subtending chord AB is 136°. Find the angle at the circumference on the same arc.
From external point P, tangent PT=12 and secant segments PA=8, PB=x. Find x.
Prove opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral sum to 180°.
Two chords intersect with segments 3,8 and 4,x. Find x and identify the theorem.

5.title: Sine and Cosine Rules; Trigonometry in Three Dimensions
tasks: In triangle ABC, a=8,b=11,C=47°. Find c and area.
Town B is due east of town A, 34 km away. Bearings of a tower from A and B are 062° and 318°. Form a triangle and find both town-to-tower distances.
Explain the ambiguous SSA case using the sine rule and sketch possibilities.
A cuboid 5×7×9 has a line from one vertex to the opposite. Find its length and angle with the base.

5.title: Vectors and Matrices
tasks: Given a=(2,−1), b=(5,3), find 3a−2b and |a+b|.
Find the matrix for reflection in y=x followed by stretch factor 2 parallel to x-axis.
Use vectors to prove the segment joining midpoints of two triangle sides is parallel to the third.
Find A⁻¹ for A=[[2,3],[1,2]] and solve A(x,y)^T=(7,4)^T.

5.title: Statistics: Dispersion, Correlation and Regression
tasks: Find population variance and standard deviation of 2,4,4,6.
A regression line y=12.4+0.83x models x within 10–40. Predict at 25 and explain why x=100 is risky.
Explain how an outlier can alter Pearson r and the regression line.
If every x is doubled and every y is changed to 3y−5, state effects on r, regression slope and intercept.

5.title: Probability: Conditional Probability and Counting
tasks: From 10 students choose president, secretary and treasurer. How many arrangements?
P(A)=0.4,P(B|A)=0.7,P(B|Aᶜ)=0.2. Find P(B) and P(A|B).
Prove Bayes’ formula from the definition of conditional probability.
How many 6-digit codes use exactly three distinct digits, with each used at least once?

5.title: Capstone: A Mathematical Modelling Project
tasks: Write a precise question for modelling daily water demand at a school. Identify response and explanatory variables.
Compare linear D=420+18n and exponential D=420(1.035)^n for n=10; state assumptions.
Design a residual check that could falsify either model.
Create a constrained optimisation model for tank size including demand uncertainty, cost and service reliability. Define every symbol.

5.title: Cumulative Revision and the Transition to DP Mathematics
tasks: Solve x²−4x−5=0, then use roots to evaluate their reciprocal sum.
A cone has fixed volume 300π. Express area in one variable and describe an optimisation route.
A claim says correlation r=0.92 proves causation. Write a mathematically rigorous critique and name two checks.
For f(x)=ln x−x/3, show there are two positive roots and locate each to intervals of width 0.1.
